Jake / team — quick legal read and suggested approach below. I applied conservative edits in-line to the redline doc (will share separate copy), but here are the core proposals so Procurement can evaluate:

1) Narrow Audit Rights: Replace broad "inspection rights" language with "Customer may request review of SOC 2 report and related artifacts, and may conduct a single annual security assessment limited to Customer's tenant and non-production staging resources, subject to Redwood's reasonable notice and coordination requirements."

2) Pen Test: Allow a single annual vendor-conducted penetration test or a customer-led assessment (with accredited third party) provided: (a) 30 days' written notice; (b) scope limited to Customer-tenant assets; (c) no access to Redwood's source code, internal logs outside tenant scope, or privileged internal tools. Redwood to be notified of findings and given 15 business days to remediate before public disclosure.

3) Evidence Exchange: Acceptable means of evidence delivery: read-only S3/Drive share, screenshots, or export bundles. We will not provide live shell access or cross-tenant data extracts. Proposed cadence:
   - Weekly snapshot for 4 weeks prior to SOC2 audit start date
   - Monthly evidence package otherwise (quarterly for lower-risk artifacts)

4) Confidentiality & Redaction: Add explicit right for Redwood to redact infrastructure-level logs and customer-identifiable metadata not relevant to the scope.

If this direction is acceptable, I'll produce short, edit-ready wording to insert into the MSA and Order Form. Happy to join the Wednesday call.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Legal — Redwood Inference
